news.title: Gianni Infantino drops FIFA World Cup private equity plan after global backlash
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has withdrawn his proposal to sell a stake in the commercial rights of the FIFA World Cup after facing widespread opposition from football bodies across the world.The decision came after several major football organisations, including UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation, opposed the proposal. FIFA also saw senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro resign, while chief operating officer Kevin Lamour publicly criticised the plan.Announcing the decision on Friday, Infantino admitted the proposal had become too divisive." Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place. Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve.

news.title: Fifa scraps proposal to sell off stakes in World Cup after widespread backlash
news.lede: Gianni ⁠Infantino issues statement on controversial plan. ‘This proposal will not proceed,’ confirms Fifa president. Gianni Infantino’s proposal to sell chunks of the World Cup to private investors has sensationally collapsed, with the Fifa president admitting the project “has created divisions of a nature that are no longer of the interest of the objective”, amid widespread anger globally. The plan had caused ructions within football around the world, leading Uefa to threaten a boycott of future Fifa tournaments if it was not shelved.

news.title: Fifa scraps controversial plan to sell stakes in World Cup
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino has scrapped his plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Facing backlash throughout the sport, a World Cup boycott from Europe ​and criticism ​from high-ranking officials inside Fifa itself, ​Infantino said the proposed Fifa Forward Enterprise project "will not proceed." The news came just days after the plan was made public, with the governing body releasing a statement "attributable to the Fifa President." "The Fifa ⁠Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our ​Fifa Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed," the statement read.

news.title: FIFA abandons $4.2-billion World Cup stake sale plan after global backlash
news.lede: FIFA has abandoned its controversial plan to sell a minority stake in its commercial operations, including the FIFA World Cup, following strong opposition from football federations and internal criticism.FIFA President Gianni Infantino announced on Friday that the proposal would not move forward after it became clear it had created divisions within the global football community." Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place," Infantino said in a statement, as quoted by Reuters." Our purpose has always been — and will always be — to unite and improve.

news.title: Football Ferns legend breaks silence on controversial call to miss 2023 Women's World Cup
news.lede: Reminder, this is a Premium article and requires a subscription to read. Former Football Ferns captain Abby Erceg, during one of her last international appearances. Former Football Ferns captain Abby Erceg has no regrets over her absence from the 2023 Fifa Women’s World Cup in New Zealand and Australia, even if it was one of the toughest decisions of her career. Erceg, who will feature as a guest player for Auckland FC’s invitational team against Chelsea Women on Saturday at Eden Park, was the biggest name missing from Jitka Klimkova’s squad three years ago.

news.title: FIFA scraps controversial deal to sell stakes in World Cup to private investors

FIFA on Friday abandoned a controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors after drawing vociferous opposition from European countries — and from its own ranks. The swift about-face marks a stunning defeat for FIFA President Gianni Infantino, who had championed a plan announced on Tuesday to create a commercial venture to capitalize on its tournaments — including the World Cup and the Club World Cup.

news.title: Infantino abandons plans to sell World Cup profits to private equity following massive pushback
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino is abandoning his divisive plan to sell World Cup profits to private equity after receiving pushback from all corners of the soccer world. Infantino’s decision came after his senior adviser who sat on a White House panel resigned and Asia’s soccer body joined Europe and North America in opposing it. Infantino had proposed creating a $20 billion company to run the World Cup with private investors including the Kushner family, but drew backlash that grew every day. UEFA’s 55-member nations agreed to boycott the World Cup and all other FIFA competitions over Infantino’s plan, followed by CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation.
